Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-18
Requested Service: Shoulder labral/instability repair, CPT 29806
Requesting Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the BCBSNM Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder labral/instability repair), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 22, 2026, Reference Number POC-6E764DFFE5-45256. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria."

I understand that BCBSNM applies its Medical Policy Manual, Surgery Policy No. SUR228, "Shoulder Surgeries," to determine medical necessity for this procedure. Section II of that policy addresses "Labral repair with or without capsulorrhaphy," and states the following medical-necessity criteria (quoted directly from the policy document I obtained):

"II. Labral repair with or without capsulorrhaphy may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.): A. Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and B. Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from an acute traumatic dislocation with imaging documenting either acute capsule-labral separation or acute bony Bankart lesion and documented recurrent episodes of instability; and C. Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates labral tear (e.g., SLAP, Bankart) and correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings; and D. All of the following are met (1. and 2.) based on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Normal or minimally limited active or passive shoulder range of motion; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests: a. O'Brien's Test; or b. Biceps Load Test; or c. Clunk Test; or d. Anterior Slide Test; or e. Compression Rotation Test; or f. Speed's Test; or g. Modified dynamic labral shear; or h. Apprehension test; or i. Anterior or posterior load and shift test; or j. Positive sulcus sign."

I believe the clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request satisfies each of these criteria, as follows:

**Criterion A – Function-limiting pain / loss of function:**
Ms./Mr. Foster has had recurrent shoulder instability for 14 months and, as a result, avoids overhead reaching and cannot return to work duties requiring lifting. This is a documented, ongoing interference with both activities of daily living and employment demands, consistent with the example given in Criterion A.

**Criterion B – Non-surgical management and/or recurrent traumatic instability (either pathway satisfied):**
- *Pathway B.1 (failure of conservative care):* The patient completed a 10-week, 20-visit supervised physical therapy program (2026-05-02 through 2026-07-11) targeting rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. The patient also completed a 6-month trial of NSAIDs during symptom flares. A corticosteroid injection was not administered because it is not clinically indicated for instability, as documented by the treating surgeon.
- *Pathway B.2 (recurrent traumatic instability):* Independently, the patient meets this second pathway: the MR arthrogram documents an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with an associated Hill-Sachs lesion, and the patient has sustained three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptom onset, with the most recent dislocation requiring emergency department reduction. This constitutes "documented recurrent episodes of instability" together with imaging-confirmed "capsule-labral separation," as described in Criterion B.2.

Because either B.1 or B.2 independently satisfies Criterion B ("Either of the following criteria are met"), the record satisfies this requirement under both pathways.

**Criterion C – Imaging correlation:**
The MR arthrogram of the shoulder performed 2026-06-12 demonstrates an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion and glenoid bone loss under 10%. This finding directly correlates with the patient's reported symptoms of recurrent instability and apprehension, and with the exam findings below.

**Criterion D – Physical examination findings:**
- D.2 (positive orthopedic test): The exam documents positive apprehension and relocation testing and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing. The apprehension test and the anterior/posterior load-and-shift test are both listed as qualifying positive orthopedic tests under Criterion D.2, and are satisfied here.
- D.1 (range of motion): The clinical record provided to me documents full strength on exam but does not separately state the active/passive range-of-motion findings compared with the uninvolved side. [Please see attached/forthcoming supplemental documentation from Dr. Lindqvist confirming range-of-motion findings, or treat this as an outstanding item the surgeon's office will supplement upon request.]

In summary, based on the policy language quoted above, the submitted clinical record meets Criteria A, B (under both alternative pathways), and C in full, and meets one of the two required elements of Criterion D, with the remaining range-of-motion documentation available upon request from the treating surgeon's office.

I am requesting that BCBSNM:
1. Reverse the denial of CPT 29806 and approve the requested labral/instability repair as medically necessary under SUR228, Section II; or, in the alternative,
2. Identify precisely which specific criterion or sub-criterion of SUR228 Section II the plan believes is not met, so that the treating surgeon can submit any additional supporting documentation (such as range-of-motion measurements) needed to complete the record; and
3. Provide a copy of the complete clinical rationale and the specific policy/criteria version actually applied to this determination, as I am entitled to receive under the plan's appeal disclosure obligations.

Enclosed with this appeal are the following supporting records:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-02 to 2026-07-11, 20 visits)
- MR arthrogram report, shoulder, dated 2026-06-12
- Emergency department record documenting reduction of anterior shoulder dislocation
- Office notes documenting three anterior dislocation episodes and 14-month symptom history
- Physical examination findings (apprehension, relocation, and load-and-shift testing)
- Medication history documenting 6-month NSAID trial
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery

[Note: I have not been provided with, and this letter does not attempt to quote, any BCBSNM-specific denial rationale beyond what appears in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination itself. If BCBSNM's internal review relied on additional or different criteria than SUR228 Section II as quoted above, I request that those specific criteria be identified in writing so that I may respond to them directly.]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and notify me and Dr. Lindqvist's office of the outcome within the timeframe required for pre-service appeals under applicable New Mexico and federal law.

If this matter is time-sensitive due to ongoing risk of further dislocation, please treat this as an expedited/urgent appeal and contact me and Dr. Lindqvist's office at the numbers below as soon as possible.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,
